his heart was moved with pity, and he gave them an assurance concerning their lives and also their possessions.
And when he entered the city, he honoured the Arab magnates who were in it,
and he brought them to his table.
And he commanded that they should take everything they could of their possessions and their weapons,
and he sent them to Antioch.
And to whoever did not wish to go to Antioch,
but to the rest of the cities of the Arabs,
he likewise sent them wherever they wished.
And he appointed three patricians with them to guard them,
and not allow anyone to harm them.
And as for certain Armenians who were insolent and laid a hand on some of the Arabs,
they cut off (he cut off?) their hands and their noses,
and he scourged them severely. And along the whole road he kept sending envoys and urging
that they should reach their fellow Arabs safely.
Now the mosque of Tarsus he made into a stable for his horses,
and he stationed a certain patrician in Tarsus with five thousand horsemen,
and likewise in Mopsuestia he placed another patrician.
And Tarsus was greatly built up and inhabited {OCR? populated},
and there was plenty in it, so that twelve pounds of bread were sold for one zuz.
And many of the Arabs who were its inhabitants returned to it;
and some were baptized and became Christians,
and others remained in their faith,
but all their children were baptized.
And after a year,
King Nicephorus came and encamped against Amid,
but was unable to subdue it.
And he went and encamped against Antioch again,
and made war against it for many days,
and likewise its strength could not be overcome.
However, he laid waste to the villages and orchards around it (that were around it),
and departed.
And after a year,
Sayf al-Dawla, the Emir of Aleppo, died of colic {OCR? apoplexy / cramp}.
And Mu'izz al-Dawla, the Emir of Baghdad, also died of the kidney disease,
and 'Izz al-Dawla his son succeeded him.
And in that year,
which was the year 356,
the year 356 of the Arabs {OCR? 256 error for 356}:
Nasir al-Dawla, the Emir of Mosul, while sleeping in his bed,
was seized by his son Abu Taghlib,
and he sent him and imprisoned {OCR?} him in the fortress of Kawashi.
And he set guards over him, a certain Kurd who hated him, and likewise another eunuch whom he had previously expelled;
and he commanded them both never to let him know any news at all.
